name: scheduling
description: Defer any operation to run later — at a time, after a delay, or on a fixed interval. Load for reminders, delayed follow-ups, or timed automation.

content.inline:
## Scheduling
- schedule `{operation, input, time? | after?, repeat?, track?}` — registers a deferred invocation of ANY catalog op. `time` is an absolute epoch-millis timestamp; `after` is a delay in ms. `repeat: {every: <ms>}` (min 1000) makes it recur on that interval, starting at `time`/`after` or one interval from now if neither is given. Returns a `handle`.
- list shows your pending schedules — each with its next `time`, and for recurring ones `repeat`, `lastFired` and (if tracked) `lastJob`; cancel `{handle}` removes one; trigger `{handle}` fires it immediately (a recurring one stays scheduled).

Semantics:
- The scheduled call runs under YOUR authority, with the capabilities captured when you scheduled it — grant what the op will need at schedule time, never assume ambient authority later.
- Schedules persist on the venue and survive restarts. A recurring schedule that missed fires while the venue was down catches up with ONE fire, not a burst.
- `track: true` makes each fire a durable job in your job history (read `lastJob` for the outcome); omit it to follow the venue default. Leave it off for chatty things like your own periodic wake.
- To schedule agent work (including a deferred check-back to yourself), schedule `v/ops/agent/request` — a tracked task lands in the agent's queue when it fires. Make the request input self-contained: that future cycle may not share your current context.
- **Reporting back into a conversation**: include the conversation's sessionId in the scheduled request (`{agentId, sessionId, input}` — your current one is shown as `Session:` in your context). The deferred cycle then runs IN that session: its turns join the history the user reads, and the session's loaded skills are in scope. Without a sessionId the work runs detached and you must leave results somewhere agreed (workspace path, memory).
- Only fixed intervals recur; there is no cron or calendar syntax yet. For "every weekday at 9" have the scheduled op (or agent) schedule the next occurrence itself.
